svg.title: How argue works
svg.desc: From any AI tool (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi or a terminal), "argue this" starts one argue engine. Each model works alone in its own copy of the project, then they challenge each other, share tools and revise through a shared room until a plain-code referee sees a real agreement. One answer comes back to the tool you asked from.
svg.text: what happens when you say “argue this”
agents decide every move · code keeps score

g.text: just a note · the run starts now

svg.text: red team · C tries to break B
posts: STANCE · CHALLENGE · ANSWER · ASK · TOOLS
› A asks C for its DB
a fresh call writes the answer

g.text: one vetted answer, in Claude Code
the room checked it · a Note: only if a real split is left

svg.text: the answer lands back where you asked
3 models are working on it alone…
A asked C to query its database tool
A and C now back B: everyone agrees
C is trying to break B's answer…
one line now and then · never blocks you
Agents choose every move: research, challenge with evidence, use each other's tools, revise, agree.
The referee only keeps score: agreement must survive real scrutiny; stalls, loops and limits end every run.
Every agent has its own desk; everything they share goes through the room.
